Remember that the eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =\lambda v \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 20-4k & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =(2k+1)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}7 \\ 26-4k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2k+1 \\ 4k+2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}7=2k+1, \\ 26-4k=4k+2\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $k$ in the first equation, we get

$$
7=2k+1\,⟹\,k=3.
$$

Now, substituting $k=3$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}26-4k & =4k+2 \\ 26-4\cdot 3 & =4\cdot 3+2 \\ 14 & =14,\end{aligned}
$$

which is a true statement.

Therefore, the solution of the system is $k=3.$
